name: inprocess-obi-ahb-sha256-f1f4
description: One Ibex RVFI OBI CPU reaches one unmodified Caliptra v2.1.2 sha256_ctrl AHB-Lite register target in one process. The target artifact states its own ahb-lite protocol, the host samples the slave port's own address phase and data phase (hsel/htrans/haddr/hwrite/hsize/hwdata/hreadyin/hreadyout/hrdata/hresp), and each case states the protocol of the target it was routed to.
notes: The target is the pinned unmodified Caliptra sha256_ctrl (third_party/caliptra_upstream_reference, revision 49370266) behind the generated ahb_lite_mmio_target manager: the generated model exposes the slave's ten declared roles as passive taps, so both AHB phases are sampled from the DUT's own pins rather than reconstructed from the host request.
The window is the profile's own 4 KiB at 0x40000000: it does not overlap the RAM image 0x10000..0x30000 and clears the 4 GiB bound.

The profile declares two active-low asynchronous resets (reset_n and cptra_pwrgood); the generated request drives both low during initialization, and debugUnlock_or_scan_mode_switch is a declared constant 0. The error/notification outputs are passive observations with no IRQ contract, so no behavior file is declared and F5 is refused by name.

Registers used: NAME0(0x00, ro, the pinned SHA256_CORE_NAME0 constant), CTRL(0x10, wo singlepulse INIT/NEXT/MODE), STATUS(0x18, ro READY/VALID/WNTZ_BUSY), BLOCK0..15(0x80..0xbc, wo) and DIGEST0..7(0x100..0x11c, ro).

F4 records write BLOCK words and CTRL; F2 records read NAME0, STATUS and the DIGEST words. The real digest read back after a written block is compared with hashlib in the evidence README, which is what makes the run more than a bus handshake.
No DMA is declared: the host's routed-DMA admission does not list the ahb-lite protocol, so an F6 record is refused by name (see runs/p2-ahb-target-20261103/README.md).
